steps.message:
You are a hydrogeologist preparing site notes for a borehole drilling team.

Station Kogam-street (Bori Metropolis). Interpreted VES layer model:

Layer | Resistivity (ohm-m) | Thickness (m) | Depth to base (m)
----- | ------------------- | ------------- | -----------------
1 | 127 | 0.822 | 0.822
2 | 50.4 | 5.63 | 6.45
3 | 126 | 21.2 | 27.7
4 | 149 | 29.7 | 57.3
5 | 197 | - | -

The survey interpretation on file classifies this sounding curve as K-type.

Write the site note using exactly this template:

Station: <station name>
Curve type: <VES curve type>
Aquifer depth: <depth range in m>
Recommendation: <one or two sentences for the drilling team>

Reference note: Curve-type notation for vertical electrical sounding (VES): take the layer resistivities in depth order. For each group of three consecutive layers (layers 1-2-3, then 2-3-4, and so on), write one letter: A if r1 < r2 < r3; Q if r1 > r2 > r3; H if r1 > r2 < r3; K if r1 < r2 > r3. A curve with N layers gets N-2 letters, in depth order (for example, a 4-layer curve gets 2 letters, such as HA). If all the letters are the same, the curve may also be written as that single letter (AAA may be written A).

Station: Kogam-street (Bori Metropolis)
Curve type: HAA — re-checking the resistivities (127 > 50.4 < 126 → H; 50.4 < 126 < 149 → A; 126 < 149 < 197 → A) gives an H‑A‑A sequence, not the K-type listed in the file; the file record should be corrected.
Aquifer depth: ≈6.45 m – 57.3 m (the moderately resistive sand sequence of layers 3–4, sandwiched beneath the shallow clay cap at 0.822–6.45 m; layer 5 below 57.3 m is still rising in resistivity and may represent a deeper, untested productive sand unit).
Recommendation: Case and grout off the 0–6.45 m clay/topsoil interval to prevent caving and cross-contamination, then screen the 6.45–57.3 m interval as the primary target zone; if higher yield is required, consider extending the borehole past 57.3 m to test the underlying higher-resistivity unit, and flag the curve-type discrepancy for re-interpretation before finalizing the design.
